chunks: “Do not recline in the bathhouse, for it melts the fat of the two kidneys. Do not comb in the bathhouse, for it thins the hair. Do not wash your head with clay, for it disfigures the face.”
And in another hadith: “It takes away ghayrah. Do not rub yourself with pottery, for it causes leprosy. Do not wipe your face with the waistcloth, for it takes away the water of the face.”

And it is narrated: “That refers to the clay of Miṣr and the pottery of al-Shām. Using the siwāk in the bathhouse causes disease of the teeth. It is not جائز to purify oneself or perform ghusl with the wastewater of the bathhouse.”

key_terms.الْبَرَصَ: leprosy; mentioned as a harmful result
key_terms.الْحَمَّامِ: the bathhouse; the setting in which these etiquettes and rulings apply
key_terms.الْغَيْرَةِ: protective jealousy/modesty; mentioned as something diminished by the practice described
key_terms.بِالطِّينِ: with clay; used here for washing the head, which is discouraged
key_terms.بِالْإِزَارِ: with the waistcloth; referring to wiping the face with it
key_terms.بِالْخَزَفِ: with pottery; referring to rubbing oneself with pottery material
key_terms.بِغُسَالَةِ الْحَمَّامِ: with the bathhouse wastewater; the substance with which purification and ghusl are said to be invalid
key_terms.شَحْمَ الْكُلْيَتَيْنِ: the fat of the two kidneys; mentioned as being affected by reclining in the bathhouse

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teach about bathhouse etiquette and purification with bathhouse wastewater?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام gives etiquette and cautions related to conduct in the bathhouse, mentioning disliked or harmful practices and their consequences. It also includes a legal ruling that purification and ghusl with the bathhouse’s wastewater are not permissible.
